# Same-source post-arrival cleanup-only V1

This narrowly selected controller addresses a verified staging arrival whose normal cleanup did not complete before its installation grant expired. It neither extends that grant nor permits installation, source writes, service restart, roles, database writes, deployment, publication or production. The original failure remains a failure. A new independent fifteen-minute certificate permits only the unchanged Python engine's removal of the retained installation `next` and consumed `packet`, with original audit retained. The live compiled tree is never selected for deletion.

The release owner must independently review this controller and pass the whole `test/cleanup-only-recovery-controls.test.ts` through the existing focused hosted diagnostic route. That diagnostic is operational controller evidence, not new application CI, compiler, staging arrival or browser acceptance. The unchanged original source's successful full CI/build/consumer evidence remains tied to its original source and runs.

## Private preparation and execution

All paths below are operator-supplied canonical private paths. Keep configuration, certificates, raw API responses, reconciliation, owner evidence and output directories outside Git, directories0700/files0600. Do not publish actual private paths, keys, lease secrets, challenges or raw private records. The six `cleanup-only-recovery-*.mjs` files form a reviewed byte-pinned bundle; copy them together into a separate private remote directory, never over the deployed source. The operator verifies every remote file hash before use. Root alone owns transfer and the actual lease.

The private config contains `frozen` (the clean original source checkout), `controller` (the reviewed new tool commit), `remoteToolDirectory`, `remoteReconciliation`, `reconciliationPath`, `reconciliationSha256`, `attemptName` (`cleanup-only-v1-...`), `out` (a NEW directory), `originalEvidence`, and, for cleanup, `certificatePath`, `remoteCertificate`, `humanEvidencePath`. The reconciliation additionally requires a nonempty `priorDiagnostics` array (at most256 entries), each with safe installation-relative `path`, `kind` (`directory` or `file`), `device`, `inode`, and for files `bytes`/`sha256`. Include every prior failed attempt directory and its complete file inventory. The reconciliation is an actual independent guarded observation: original installer absent, both owned trees intact, every original failed diagnostic and original verified/activated record bytes/hash/inodes retained, and no authority/consume/result/lock. The server refuses existing state rather than stealing or overwriting it. Root must freshly reconcile all failed attempt directories as well as canonical records; private evidence must retain their identities.

1. Run `node --import tsx .github/ci/cleanup-only-recovery-operator.mjs inspect PRIVATE_CONFIG`. This is READ ONLY under the actual existing same-source batch/epoch guard and exclusive cleanup lock. It lifts the original installer runtime/source/compiled inventory contracts, verifies full636 ledger/health/current PID/boot/environment, and captures complete metadata fences before/after full audit. It does not treat the expired grant as permission or write an authority.
2. Immediately run `node --import tsx .github/ci/cleanup-only-recovery-admission.mjs reauthenticate ORIGINAL_CHECKOUT ORIGINAL_VERIFICATION_JSON NEW_REAUTH_JSON`. It invokes the frozen original authenticated CI verifier, then obtains actual original run/artifact/main/alpha API metadata and retains its hash. No CI dispatch or retest occurs.
3. Run `node .github/ci/cleanup-only-recovery-admission.mjs issue NEW_REAUTH_JSON NEW_INSPECTION_JSON EXISTING_OWNER_EVIDENCE TOOL_COMMIT NEW_CERTIFICATE`. Existing owner evidence must truthfully document the user's already explicit staging/owned-cleanup/autonomous authorization, not invent a new approval. Both inspection and reauthentication must be at most120seconds old at issuance. The exact certificate binds original source/install/build/CI artifact, new tool/controller bytes, owner-evidence hash, full runtime and fresh fences. Runtime binding removes ONLY the two observation-time fields (runtime.verifiedAt and migrationLedger.verifiedAt); pre/post full audit hashes must otherwise match the issued binding exactly, including compiled inventory and every ledger field. Its new fifteen-minute lifetime is independent of the expired original grant, which remains immutable metadata.
4. Root transfers the exact private certificate separately under the actual guard and selects a NEW local output directory in the cleanup config. Run `node --import tsx .github/ci/cleanup-only-recovery-operator.mjs cleanup PRIVATE_CONFIG`.

The server validates the new certificate before every phase, preserves original bytes/inodes, performs another full pre-audit, then issues a fresh nonce/READY. The operator may wait at most2seconds of REAL wallclock for a slightly future timestamp, without changing either clock or validation time. The unchanged READY180seconds/source checksum60seconds bounds apply. A fresh actual canonical rsync checksum must be empty before COMMIT; all source/compiled/record/lease/PID/boot/environment/ledger fences must remain identical. New canonical authority/consumption use exclusive creation only. The engine runs once, followed by another complete runtime/636/compiled audit. Any incomplete transport, drift, expiry or prior consumption refuses and requires reconciliation, never an automatic retry.

The client reuses the original final cleanup/arrival validator only as a structural projection of the NEW purpose-specific proof, with expired grant as metadata, then requires a final actual canonical zero source checksum and still-valid new certificate. The distinct composed receipt preserves original operator exit1, original failed receipt hash, original installed-arrival hash and full original CI identity. It is not a claim that the original wrapper passed. Root separately owns lease phase, post-arrival catalog/ACL checks and actual authorized/denied/replay rendered acceptance. No native positive or authenticated business authorization is inferred from cleanup, health, static bytes or tenant-only probes.

## Preserved controls and limits

No original guard, installer, Python engine, workflow, package, SQL, provider binding or application test is changed. Full audits are read-only metadata and byte verification, not application tests or builds. The read-only runtime lift intentionally uses the expired grant only for immutable build/origin comparison; its permission callback validates the new cleanup certificate and active lease. It can never activate/install. The actual root must confirm source/CI witness policy freshness and shared queue/lease authority before invoking this operator. If current policy cannot admit a new cleanup-only purpose, stop for the actual policy decision rather than misusing the expired installation grant.
